process.title: Process
process.scoreBody: Drills and planned rounds, graded independently of the outcome.

guide.title: Five moves, no heroics.
guide.subtitle: Blind replay is not a prediction game. It is a rehearsal of five behaviours you can repeat when the ticker is visible and the money is real.

read.title: Read the state before the trade.
read.body: Mark the last three swings. Higher highs and higher lows is an uptrend; lower highs and lower lows is a downtrend. If neither is true, you are in a range until proven otherwise.
read.body2: Disorder is not a range. Wide, overlapping bars with no clean swing sequence mean there is no structural trade — and standing aside is the correct output.
read.b1: Call the state in one sentence before you look at the size field.
read.b2: Trend trades only go with the trend; counter-trend clicks are locked while you call a trend.
read.b3: When the state is unclear, choose Disorder and wait.
read.note:
HH / HL → uptrend
LH / LL → downtrend
Overlap → range
Violent overlap → disorder

invalidation.title: Place the invalidation before the entry.
invalidation.body: A stop is a statement about where your idea is wrong, not how much you are willing to lose. Put it beyond the swing that would invalidate the structure, then compute the size.
invalidation.body2: If the structural stop is wider than the risk budget allows, the trade is too big. The answer is to skip it or trade fewer contracts — never to tighten the stop into noise.
invalidation.b1: Stop beyond the last swing low/high or the range edge.
invalidation.b2: Target at the next structure, not at a round number.
invalidation.b3: A 1.5R floor keeps the math honest; beyond 8R, ask what structure supports it.
invalidation.note:
long: stop < entry < target
short: target < entry < stop
distance in ATR and ticks

sizing.title: Size by risk, not by conviction.
sizing.body: Contracts = risk budget / (stop ticks × tick value + round-turn fees). The app derives this for you, but you should be able to do it on a napkin for the contracts you trade.
sizing.body2: Leverage is an output, not an input. A wider stop is not a reason to add size; it is a reason to own fewer contracts.
sizing.b1: Default budget: 1% of the account per trade.
sizing.b2: Fees count toward risk. A high-frequency plan is a smaller plan.
sizing.b3: Max contracts is a hard cap, even when the math says more.
sizing.note:
contracts = floor(budget ÷ risk per contract)
MNQ: 40 ticks × $0.50 + $1.24
    = $21.24 per contract

tape.title: Let the tape speak.
tape.body: Once the bracket is live, the only job is to manage what the market gives you. No rewinds, no adding indicators, no moving the stop because the bar looks scary.
tape.body2: The replay prints one candle at a time for a reason: it removes the hindsight that makes every chart look obvious.
tape.b1: Space plays or pauses; N steps one bar.
tape.b2: A working limit order fills at the level or better; gaps fill at the open.
tape.b3: If a bar touches both stop and target, the simulator assumes the stop first.
tape.note:
Fills are conservative by design.
The review should not flatter you.

grading.title: Grade the process, then the P&L.
grading.body: The drill scores four things: state (40), direction (20), plan structure (25) and discipline (15). The outcome is reported separately, so a lucky win cannot hide a counter-trend entry.
grading.body2: A losing trade with the right read, a structural stop and the risk cap respected can still grade A. That is the behaviour that survives an evaluation.
grading.b1: State is graded against the hidden regime.
grading.b2: Plan structure rewards stops beyond swings and realistic R:R.
grading.b3: Waiting at least three bars before acting earns discipline points.
grading.note:
process 100
outcome R
A good process with a bad outcome
is still a good rep.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.r: One unit of risk. +2R means the trade made twice what the stop risked, fees included.
glossary.atr: Average true range over 14 bars. Used to measure stop and target distance in noise units.
glossary.drawdown: The distance from your equity high-water mark that the account is allowed to give back before it fails.
glossary.bracket: An entry with a stop and a target attached. One order, three prices, defined risk.
glossary.noFill: The limit entry was never touched. No position, no fee, and a valid answer.
glossary.process: The 100-point grade for state, direction, plan structure and discipline, independent of P&L.

disclaimer.title: Simulated data, not advice.
disclaimer.body: Every series is generated deterministically from a hidden seed. There is no broker connection, no live market feed and no promise of payouts. Prop Desk is practice software.
